draft.title: Cubic and polynomial graphs
card: A cubic such as y = (x − 1)(x + 2)(x − 3) has roots where each factor is zero: x = 1, −2 and 3. The graph crosses the x-axis at each of these.
For the y-intercept, put x = 0. Here y = (−1)(2)(−3) = 6, so the graph meets the y-axis at (0, 6).
Look at the sign of the x³ term. If it is positive, the graph rises on the right and falls on the left. If it is negative, it falls on the right and rises on the left.
A repeated factor, such as (x − 2)², gives a repeated root. The graph touches the x-axis there and turns back, instead of crossing.
draft.remember: Roots give the x-intercepts, x = 0 gives the y-intercept, and the x³ sign gives the ends. A repeated root touches.

a.q: The graph of y = (x − 2)²(x + 1) is sketched. What happens at x = 2?
opts: It touches the x-axis and turns back
It has a gap in the graph
a.why: The factor (x − 2) appears twice, so x = 2 is a repeated root and the graph touches the axis there. It crosses only at the single root x = −1. Crossing at every root is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Look at how many times the factor (x − 2) appears.

b.q: What is the y-intercept of y = −(x − 1)(x + 4)(x − 2)?
b.why: Put x = 0: y = −(−1)(4)(−2) = −8. Here (−1)(4)(−2) = 8, and the minus sign in front makes it −8. Dropping that sign gives 8, which is wrong.
b.clue: Put x = 0 and keep the minus sign at the front.

a.best: It touches the x-axis and turns back

problems.detail: The card says any repeated factor makes the graph touch the x-axis and turn back. That is only true for an even power such as (x − 2)². A cubed factor such as (x − 2)³ is also a repeated root, but the graph crosses there, flattening as it passes through. The card should say a squared (double) root touches.
"A repeated root touches" is false for a triple root such as (x − 2)³, where the graph crosses the axis. It should say a double or squared root touches.

check.summary: Both questions and their explanations are correct. The card and remember line say every repeated root touches the axis, which is wrong for a triple root like (x − 2)³, so they should say a squared (double) root.
